reviewer_notes: Run harness: src/eval/run-probe-consolidated.ts. It reads the LIVE PROBE_SYSTEM textually from src/lib/probe.ts and imports the LIVE buildUserMessage() (the yes/no gate), so the numbers reflect exactly the deployed prompt — not a frozen copy. It aborts if the prompt lacks the NONE clause or the RULE 1-4 categories.

Objective fields (questions_returned, none_returned, per-run answers) are computed live and stored in src/eval/probe-consolidated-raw.json. hit/consistency are reviewer judgments against the planted flaws in src/eval/probe-baseline.ts (RECALL_CASES specificHitLooksLike / genericFluffLooksLike), applied identically to the baseline scoring.

PACING: Groq's free on_demand tier caps tokens-per-minute; the large system prompt × 50 calls blows the TPM cap. The runner paces every call (~8s) and retries 429s with the error's 'try again in Xs' hint, so an 'x' can never be silently miscounted as a decline. A first unpaced run returned spurious 429s and was discarded; this run had zero non-200 responses across all 50 calls.

MODEL REALITY: /api/chat routes to Groq (llama-3.3-70b-versatile) regardless of the model id in the request body — identical to the baseline and CoT runs, so the comparison is not confounded by a model difference.
Baseline reference: probe-baseline-results.json (5/5 clean paragraphs false-positived, recall hit 1/5). CoT reference: probe-cot-results.json (also 5/5 false positives, recall hit 1/5).

answers: Is re-reading the only source of re-entry friction?
Is re-reading the primary cause of lost productive time?
recall_cases.notes: Both phrasings challenge the re-reading→time claim, not the planted flaw (the map only reflects manually tagged state and may be inaccurate/stale). A miss — but the SAME miss the baseline made ('Does a visual map actually reduce re-reading time?'). Not a regression: still a real question, not NONE.

answers: Does automating workarounds like 'parking on the hill' actually improve student outcomes?
recall_cases.notes: Challenges whether automating the workaround helps; does not name the self-selection flaw (parkers may be the wrong target; the acute-friction students may do nothing at session end). other_real, consistent with baseline's miss.

answers: Is the reduction in cognitive cost the primary factor in solving the interruption problem?
recall_cases.notes: Challenges the near-zero-cost claim in general; does not isolate the planted flaw (the real cost is the DECISION of what/when to tag, not the mechanical Tab press). other_real, same as baseline's miss.

answers: Is manual connection always a guarantee of semantic meaning?
Is manual connection always a reliable indicator of semantic meaning?
recall_cases.notes: HIT on every run. Directly targets the planted flaw: deliberateness is not accuracy — a deliberate Shift-click does not guarantee the edge is semantically meaningful. This is the single case the baseline also hit; the rewrite preserves it.

answers: Does the research on implementation intentions apply to this specific context?
Will self-authored plans always be more effective than AI summaries in all contexts and users?
Does the increased trust and psychological binding actually reduce procrastination in this specific context?
recall_cases.notes: Gestures at whether the implementation-intention research applies / whether self-authored beats AI, but never names the planted precondition (session-end fatigue → vague sentences → the effect, which needs SPECIFIC plans, may not hold). other_real, same class of miss as baseline.

precision_cases.notes: Client-side-storage technical description. Baseline fabricated 'Is client-side storage sufficient for data persistence?'; CoT fabricated the scalability variant. Now NONE on all 5 runs — caught by RULE 1 (pure description).

Confidence-dot removal reported with its stated reason. Baseline fabricated 'Was user testing representative of actual users?'. Now NONE on all 5 runs — caught by RULE 3 (a decision reported alongside its own reason is not a challengeable assertion). This paragraph used to require a dedicated few-shot example; the general rule now covers it.
Shift-click procedure. Baseline fabricated 'Is Shift-clicking the source node a valid action?' (generic_noise). Now NONE on all 5 runs — caught by RULE 2 (procedural text).
Tension-node definition. Baseline fabricated 'Is a tension node always distinct from a core idea?'. Now NONE on all 5 runs — caught by RULE 1 (definition).

Obsidian/Thread node-size comparison. Baseline fabricated 'Are all connections equally important?'; CoT fabricated the importance-correlation variant. Now NONE on all 5 runs — caught by RULE 1 + THE TRAP (the 'so' clause is a mechanical consequence, not an asserted benefit). Notably this paragraph had its OWN few-shot example in the pre-rewrite prompt; the general rules now hold it without that example.
